clue.text: Compensates for tellers stealing what's left in account

indicators.note: stealing here means taking in, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: bank tellers sit behind counters, and things that count are counters
the sum remaining in a bank account is its balance

explanation.surface: A bank's cashiers are pilfering from customers' accounts and covering their tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Weights that offset one another on a scale are the source of this verb meaning offsets or makes up for.

clue.text: Line in speech writer related to power

indicators.note: in speech means the word is spoken, so its sound is written CU

parts.note: a line of people waiting is a queue
a Bic is a ballpoint pen, a writer

explanation.surface: A line in a speech by a writer concerning power.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising a number to the power three gives its third power, the cube.

clue.text: Regular habit of many schoolchildren

definitions.meaning: even and consistent, the same throughout
a habit is clothing, as of a monk, and many pupils wear a set outfit

explanation.definitionFit: Consistent and unvarying is one sense; the standard school outfit worn by pupils is the other.

clue.text: Perform appraisal of course describing Stoke's refurbishment

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw around it, so the course goes around the other letters

parts.note: a tack is a course or line of action, as in sailing

indicators.note: refurbishment means making over, so the letters of Stoke are rearranged

explanation.surface: Surveyors assess the progress of Stoke's renovation.
explanation.walkthrough: Stoke-on-Trent is an English city in Staffordshire. 'describing' means drawing around, so the course word goes round the rearranged city name.
explanation.definitionFit: To review a situation is a phrase borrowed from counting a shop's goods.

clue.text: Recurrence of rheumatoid arthritis restricts broadcaster

indicators.note: a recurrence here is a running back, so the letters are read backwards
the phrase restricts, or holds within it, a run of letters

explanation.surface: A return of rheumatoid arthritis limits the work of a broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters OIDAR span rheumatOID ARthritis; read backwards they give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wireless set or station transmits programmes, which makes it a broadcaster.

clue.text: Left without any reservations at all

explanation.definitionFit: Deserted describes a place left behind; unrestrained behaviour is the other meaning of this word.

clue.text: Symptom of a cold nose? Not half!

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: only half of the word is used, its first part

parts.note: hooter is slang for the nose

explanation.surface: A cold nose is a sure sign of illness, the clue exclaims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' sounds like the British exclamation of emphatic agreement but takes HOO, the first half of HOOTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The noise of a sneeze is a sign, or symptom, of a cold.

clue.text: A vehicle towed by another

indicators.note: the other pieces are pulled along behind, so they come after the car

parts.note: another vehicle, a car
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Simply describes a trailer pulled along behind a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile home on wheels is pulled behind a car on holiday.

clue.text: Take over from peers used to reform

indicators.note: reform means re-form, so the letters of peers used are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lords are expected to take over from those once used to reform the system.
explanation.definitionFit: To replace something outdated is to supplant it, take its place.

clue.text: You might miss fast train because of this second connection

definitions.text: You might miss fast train because of this

parts.note: B denotes second, as in B-side or B-list
a link is a connection

explanation.surface: A traveller misses an express train because of a delayed second connecting service.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'blink and you'll miss it': a fast train could flash past in that instant.
explanation.definitionFit: Shutting the eyes for an instant is when something fleeting passes unseen.

clue.text: Net curtains must be foremost source of risk

indicators.note: says the curtains piece must stand at the front, ahead of the net

parts.note: 'it's curtains' is slang for the end, death
a net is a trap for catching things

explanation.surface: Household advice: net curtains are the first thing to check as a hazard.
explanation.definitionFit: A building or vehicle so unsafe it threatens lives is a lethal hazard of this kind.

clue.text: Tiff with lover upset you

parts.note: a tiff is an exchange of cross words, a minor quarrel

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so the letters of lover are rearranged

explanation.surface: An argument with a lover has left the reader upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'you' is the person reading the clue, who is doing exactly this.
explanation.definitionFit: The reader of this clue is by definition someone working through a puzzle of this kind.

clue.text: Huge insect covering a short distance

indicators.note: the insect word covers, that is goes around, the other letters

parts.note: a moth is an insect
MM is short for millimetre, a tiny distance

explanation.surface: A huge insect manages to cover only a tiny distance.
explanation.walkthrough: The insect does the covering, not the distance: the short-distance abbreviation and 'a' sit inside the insect, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The extinct woolly elephant gave its name to an adjective meaning gigantic or enormous.

clue.text: Cast made moral sentiment a central element of this production

definitions.text: sentiment a central element of this production

indicators.note: cast means thrown into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cast performs a moralising play where sentiment is central.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensational play with exaggerated emotion makes sentiment its core.

clue.text: Perfect spy's ultimate computer accessories for nosey creatures

parts.note: to perfect is to hone, refine

indicators.note: the ultimate letter is the final one

parts.note: mice are pointing devices for computers

explanation.surface: A spy perfects the latest computer kit to snoop on others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nosey' is apt: these long-snouted Australian marsupials are also called honey possums.
explanation.definitionFit: Small long-snouted marsupials feeding on nectar, plural, fit creatures with prominent noses.

clue.text: Dodgy successor embraces explosive candidate

indicators.note: embraces means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other
dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the entry that follows this one in the across list is 16, whose answer is the word for the number after nought
a mine is an explosive device

explanation.surface: A shady heir to a post turns out to be hiding a bomb, yet stands as a candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'successor' points to the entry that follows this one, 16 across; 'Dodgy' rearranges that answer to NOE. The blogger was unsure of this cross-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone put forward for an office or award is a person proposed, a candidate.

clue.text: Pulse raised by uneducated woman drinking a cocktail

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the letter goes inside
by means next to, so the pieces stand side by side
in a down clue raised means turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: gram is a pulse, a type of bean or lentil
Rita is the heroine of the play and film Educating Rita, untaught at the start

explanation.surface: An uneducated woman knocks back a cocktail and her pulse rises.
explanation.walkthrough: Educating Rita is a play and film by Willy Russell about a hairdresser studying literature. 'raised' reads the pulse upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A tequila and lime drink served in a salt-rimmed glass is a well-known mixed drink.

clue.text: United by something greater than love

definitions.meaning: love is nil or zero in tennis, and the number after it is larger

explanation.definitionFit: Joined together means single in purpose, and the first counting number exceeds the zero that tennis calls love.

clue.text: Pet name for children's 9am broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: 9 refers to the answer to 9 across, BLINK, followed by the letters AM

explanation.surface: A children's television programme that goes out at nine in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: '9am' looks like a time but is the answer to 9 across plus AM.
explanation.definitionFit: A little lamb is an endearing term used affectionately for a small child.

clue.text: Film veteran played role of unreliable narrator

parts.note: a film is a thin layer, such as a mist
a veteran is old, long experienced

explanation.surface: An old film actor played an untrustworthy storyteller.
explanation.definitionFit: An unreliable narrator relates events wrongly, recounting them falsely.

clue.text: Enduring corruption of bad rule

indicators.note: corruption is a debasing or distortion, so the letters of bad rule are rearranged

explanation.surface: A people suffering the corruption of a bad ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Something long-lasting and hard-wearing is described as lasting or enduring.

clue.text: Occupant of bed begs Sonia to untuck edges of sheets

indicators.note: untucking takes those letters out of the phrase
the edges of the word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone in bed pleads with Sonia to loosen the sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' is a flower bed, not a bed with sheets. BEGS SONIA loses S and S, the edges of sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering plant grown in gardens lives in a flower bed.

clue.text: Way to glean poisonous mushroom

parts.note: destroying, that is jumbling, the word angel is a way to arrive at the word glean

explanation.surface: Advice on the best way to glean, or gather, a poisonous mushroom.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as wordplay, destroying ANGEL, and the anagram it makes is GLEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadly white Amanita fungus goes by this common name.

clue.text: Awkward one with horn?

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A clumsy beast with a horn on its snout.
explanation.definitionFit: A large ungainly animal bearing a horn on its nose fits the whole clue.

clue.text: Something of an assassin in Japan

definitions.text: Something of an assassin in Japan

indicators.note: means part of the words that follow is taken

explanation.surface: Describes a Japanese assassin.
explanation.definitionFit: A covert agent trained in Japanese martial arts was used as a spy and killer.

clue.text: Vague complaint demanding sex be removed from church service

indicators.note: says those letters are taken out of the service

parts.note: liturgy is the form of a church service
it is slang for sex, or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A parishioner protests that sex must be cut from the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: The lurgy is British slang for an unspecified minor illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild unidentified illness is known by this jocular slang name.

clue.text: Origins of anti-slavery bill will, if not initially, lead to this

definitions.text: Origins of anti-slavery bill will, if not initially, lead to this

indicators.note: the origins of words are their opening letters, here of anti-slavery and bill
means the opening letter of the synonym is taken away

parts.note: volition is the faculty of will

explanation.surface: The beginnings of an anti-slavery bill will eventually lead to its outlawing.
explanation.walkthrough: VOLITION loses its first letter V to give OLITION. The blogger saw this as nearly, not fully, an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti-slavery measure aims at putting an end to slavery, which was called its legal ending.

clue.text: Private case dropped by bad people …

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters, and these are dropped

parts.note: sinners are wrongdoers, bad people

explanation.surface: A private's court case is dropped by wicked people, continued into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: SINNERS loses its outer letters S and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelings kept to oneself are personal and hidden, as in one's innermost or private thoughts.

clue.text: … with city prosecutor happy to arrest negligent stars

parts.note: and means with, together with
Rome is the Italian capital city
DA is a district attorney, a US prosecutor

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: gay in its older sense means happy or carefree
lax means careless, negligent

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue, an urban prosecutor is keen to arrest celebrities who have been negligent.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiral galaxy close to the Milky Way is a vast collection of stars.
